title: The completed proper/open value is a derived limit of its finite compact-support tower
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l, and a global finite-field datum D with l invertible in its algebraic closure k [def-pur-conventions]. Let f:X -> Y be separated and finite type between separated finite-type k-schemes, and choose a compactification c=(j,p) [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Let M be a derived-complete integral constructible completed-coefficient object whose finite reductions have one uniform finite Tor interval [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. With the completed proper/open functor image (completed l E) c [def-pur-integral-compact-support-coefficient-data], and the finite support terms sfCompactSupportTerm l E c M n and quotient-induced adjacent transitions sfCompactSupportTransition l E c M n [def-sf-integral-compact-support-tower], the object Rp_* j_! M is a derived limit of that tower [def-weil-derived-limit]. Here n means exponent n+1, all finite coefficient actions and transitions are retained, and the derived category has the canonical countable products. Only a derived-limit triangle is asserted, with no projection normalization or uniqueness of a comparison. No varying coefficient extension, scalar-domain preservation or invertibility of a scalar mate is part of this assertion.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.13, Definition 6.7.6 and Lemma 6.7.7; the explicit strict quotient-tower and Roos argument below is an agent auxiliary, also using Stacks Tag 0941.

proof.text: Write R_W for the completed integral coefficient sheaf and A_n for the constant quotient at exponent n+1. The input is derived complete by its constructible finite-Tor hypothesis. Its canonical quotient units and quotient transitions give a strict augmented reduction system whose total derived limit is M. Keep this entire system, not merely the list of its derived evaluations.

The compactification middle scheme is finite type over the base field and hence Noetherian and quasi-compact. Its open immersion is quasi-compact. In the ringed open-slice presentation, extension by zero is exact and preserves countable products. Bhatt--Scholze Lemma 6.1.13 proves the corresponding homotopy-limit assertion by the open/closed localization triangle. Apply this to the strict input reduction system. The canonical coefficient tensor/open identifications identify the result with the finite open extensions, including their quotient-unit augmentation and all transitions. Thus completed open extension of M is the total derived limit of that strict finite-open system.

Apply the separately derived proper direct image Rp_* to the preceding identification. Its normalized right-adjoint comparison commutes with total derived inverse limits. On a strict K-injective tower it is computed by applying the direct-image functor to the limit projections. Hence the resulting object is the ambient proper/open image of M, and the tower terms are the proper images of the finite open extensions.

Transport each term through the constant/quotient coefficient realization. The slice-to-intrinsic proper and open presentation comparisons form an isomorphism of whole inverse systems: finite coefficient restriction mates preserve the adjunction units, and adjacent transition equations extend to every comparable pair. This identifies that system with sfCompactSupportTerm and sfCompactSupportTransition for the given compactification and input.

Use the strict Roos comparison to compute the total limit by the shifted cone of one minus the transition shift. The system isomorphism from the previous step induces the product isomorphism intertwining these endomorphisms. Transport the resulting distinguished Roos triangle to the displayed finite-support tower. Its first vertex is the ambient proper/open image, which is exactly the asserted IsDerivedLimit. The proof asserts neither a unique triangle extension nor faithfulness of finite derived evaluation. Zero input, empty open and identity compactifications use the same constructions.

theorem integralProperOpen_isDerivedLimit
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (hunit : IsUnit (l : D.k))
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of D.k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [IsSeparated (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [f.IsOver (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (c : Compactification f)
    (M : DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource l E X))
    (hM : finiteTorConstructibleIntegral l E X M) :
    letI : HasCountableProducts (DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource l E Y)) :=
      integralOperationsDerivedCountableProducts l E Y
    IsDerivedLimit (fun n : ℕ ↦ sfCompactSupportTransition l E c M n)
      ((image (completed l E) c).obj M)
